Implement a mechanism to detect and report idle server processes in Accumulo clusters, and enable custom tagging of metrics for better observability. Ensure that server processes emit an idle metric after a configurable idle period and support custom key-value tags on all metrics.

*   Define a constant `METRICS_SERVER_IDLE` with the value `'accumulo.server.idle'` in the `MetricsProducer` interface located at `core/src/main/java/org/apache/accumulo/core/metrics/MetricsProducer.java`.
*   Add configuration properties to the `Property` enum in `core/src/main/java/org/apache/accumulo/core/conf/Property.java`:
    *   `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL` with the key `'general.metrics.process.idle'` to specify the idle duration before emitting the idle metric. It should accept time duration values.
    *   `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` with the key `'general.micrometer.user.tags'` to accept a comma-separated list of 'key=value' pairs for tagging metrics.
*   Ensure all metrics emitted by server processes include a `process.name` tag:
    *   Use `'tserver'` for tablet servers.
    *   Use `'sserver'` for scan servers.
    *   Use `'compactor'` for compactors.
*   Implement the emission of the `accumulo.server.idle` metric for tablet servers, scan servers, and compactors when they have been idle for the duration specified by `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL`. Tag these metrics with the appropriate `process.name`.
*   Ensure the `accumulo.server.idle` metric is not emitted during normal active operations.
*   When `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` is configured, append the specified tags to all metrics emitted by server processes.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Here's what I found about the Apache Accumulo idle process metric, `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL`, and the related `updateIdleStatus`/`AbstractServer` machinery.

## Origin of the feature

The idle process metric was originally introduced on the `elasticity` branch. A commit by Dave Marion on Jan 2, 2024 (PR #4078) added a counter that is incremented when the server process is idle for the duration specified by the property `general.metrics.process.idle`. The same change also added the property `general.micrometer.user.tags` that allows the user to specify additional tags to be emitted with each metric from the process.

This original PR touched `Property.java`, `MetricsProducer.java`, `MetricsUtil.java`, `AbstractServer.java`, `ProcessMetrics.java`, `Compactor.java`, `ScanServer.java`, `TabletServer.java`, and added an `IdleProcessMetricsIT` integration test.

## The property definition

The relevant property is defined as: `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL("general.metrics.process.idle", "5m", PropertyType.TIMEDURATION, "Amount of time a process must be idle before the accumulo.server.idle metric is incremented.")`

## The metric name and backport to 2.1

The feature was later backported to the 2.1 branch. In PR #4716 ("backport server idle metric to 2.1"), the changes from the idle stop PR #4078 were backported, the idle metric was converted from a Counter to a Gauge, and the COMPACTOR_BUSY metric was removed as a duplicate of this one. As part of that work, the metric constant was defined: `String METRICS_SERVER_IDLE = "accumulo.server.idle";` and the `METRICS_COMPACTOR_BUSY = METRICS_COMPACTOR_PREFIX + "busy"` constant was removed. The gauge's value will be 0 when idle and 1 when busy.

## The `updateIdleStatus` refactor

Originally the method was called `idleProcessCheck()` and took a `Supplier<Boolean>`. A PR simplified the Compactor's idle check: this PR simplifies the check for the Compactor that is used to determine when to change the idle process metric for the Compactor — the new code just returns true when no compaction is running and false when one is, deferring the time-checking portion to the upstream logic in `AbstractServer`.

The motivation was to remove duplicated and unsafe logic. The old approach checked how much time had passed since the last compaction, which had issues: there was logic ensuring the amount of time since the last compaction happened is at least `idleReportingPeriodNanos`, but this check also happens upstream when the `Supplier<boolean>` is read in `AbstractServer`, making it a duplicate. Additionally, there was a check that the `System.nanoTime()` value of the last completed compaction is not negative, which is not a safe check since `System.nanoTime()` may provide a negative value.

In a related follow-up, the method was renamed and its signature changed: `AbstractServer.updateIdleStatus()` was changed from having `Supplier<Boolean>` as its input to just a `boolean` — done to simplify things since the method was just using it as a boolean anyway. As part of the same change, the method was renamed from `idleProcessCheck()` to `updateIdleStatus()`, the idle check in `Compactor` was simplified to just set the idle status to true or false during its operation, and test cases were added to ensure that the idle metric for Compactor and ScanServer behave as expected. Notably, Tserver was omitted since it is not expected to be idle in 2.1.

## Usage in ScanServer

In `ScanServer`, the idle status is updated in the main server loop based on scan activity — the code calls `updateIdleStatus` with a condition checking whether the session manager's active scans are empty and the tablet metadata cache estimated size is 0.

## Later readability improvements

The timekeeping code was subsequently cleaned up. In PR #4737, "Improve readability of timekeeping code in idle server check" was merged into the 3.1 branch on Sept 11, 2024, modifying `AbstractServer.java` (15 insertions, 13 deletions) and updating it to use a `Timer` object.

## Even later exit-code work

The `updateIdleStatus` method also appears in later process-exit work. In the `ExitCodesIT` test, for the COMPACTOR server type the `Compactor.class` is used with the method name `"updateIdleStatus"`, which was part of PR #5811 ("Fixes for process exit, added ExitCodesIT") on the main branch, where the server loops in `ScanServer` and `Compactor` were restructured around `isShutdownRequested()`.

**Summary of the evolution:** The idle metric started as a counter (PR #4078, elasticity branch, Jan 2024) → was backported to 2.1 and converted to a 0/1 gauge named `accumulo.server.idle`, removing the duplicate `accumulo.compactor.busy` metric (PR #4716) → the Compactor's idle check was simplified and `idleProcessCheck()` was renamed to `updateIdleStatus()` taking a plain `boolean` (PRs #4740/#4716) → timekeeping readability was improved using a `Timer` (PR #4737) → later reused in process-exit testing (PR #5811).

## Summary

I implemented the idle-process detection and custom metric tagging feature, matching the upstream Accumulo design (PR #4078 on the elasticity branch), touching only source files:

**Configuration & constants**
- `MetricsProducer.java`: added `String METRICS_SERVER_IDLE = "accumulo.server.idle";`.
- `Property.java`: added `GENERAL_IDLE_PROCESS_INTERVAL` (`general.metrics.process.idle`, `TIMEDURATION`, default `5m`) and `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` (`general.micrometer.user.tags`, `STRING`).

**Tagging (`MetricsUtil.java`)**
- The public `initializeMetrics` now reads `GENERAL_MICROMETER_USER_TAGS` and passes it to the private overload, which parses the comma-separated `key=value` list and appends each valid pair as a common `Tag` on all metrics (logging a warning for malformed entries). The `process.name` tag was already applied from each server's application name.

**Idle metric emission**
- `ProcessMetrics.java`: registers an `accumulo.server.idle` counter with common tags and exposes `incrementIdleCounter()`. The low-memory gauge now also carries common tags.
- `AbstractServer.java`: reads the idle interval into `idleReportingPeriodNanos` and adds `idleProcessCheck(Supplier<Boolean>)`, which increments the idle counter once a process has continuously satisfied its idle condition for the configured duration (and resets when active — so nothing is emitted during normal operation).
- `Compactor.java`: idle when no compaction has run within the interval (tagged `process.name=compactor`).
- `ScanServer.java`: idle when there are no active scans and the tablet-metadata cache is empty (`process.name=sserver`).
- `TabletServer.java`: idle when no tablets are online (`process.name=tserver`).

**Verification**: `core`, `server/base`, `server/compactor`, and `server/tserver` all compile cleanly. No files under `tests/` were modified.
